sentiment.rationale: Guidance was raised: full-year adjusted EPS outlook increased to $17.80-$19.00 from $17.20-$19.00, and revenue growth forecast raised to 5%-6% from 4%-6%. The raise is organic, driven by strong US domestic package yield and volume, not attributed to one-time items. However, the raise is modest and accompanied by explicit headwinds (MD-11 grounding, higher incentive comp, LTL weakness) that cap the upside, preventing a higher score.

summary.revenue: Q2 revenue $23.5 billion, up 7% year-over-year (from $22.0 billion).
summary.eps: Q2 adjusted diluted EPS $4.82, up 19% year-over-year (from $4.05).
summary.guidance: FY2026 adjusted EPS raised to $17.80-$19.00 (from $17.20-$19.00); revenue growth raised to 5%-6% (from 4%-6%); pension contributions lowered to $275 million (from up to $400 million); reaffirmed $1B cost savings, ~25% ETR, $4.5B CapEx.
summary.margin: Q2 adjusted operating margin 6.9%, up 60 bps year-over-year (from 6.3%).
key_risks: MD-11 fleet grounding: $25M impact in Q2, ~$150M-$175M expected in Q3, return to service not expected until Q4.
Global trade policy changes: $1B headwind to adjusted operating profit for FY2026.
FedEx Freight weakness: adjusted operating income expected to decline $300M (worsened from $100M prior), driven by lower shipments and $100M in separation costs.
Higher variable incentive compensation: ~$265M headwind in H2 vs. prior year.
Expiration of Postal Service contract: $30M headwind in Q2.
International export volume pressure, especially China-to-US lane.
key_opportunities: US domestic package volume growth: average daily volume up 6% in Q2.
Yield improvement: US domestic package yield up >5%, international export package yield up 3%.
B2B growth: nearly half of revenue growth from B2B services; healthcare and data center verticals identified.
Network 2.0 transformation: 24% of volume through optimized facilities, targeting 65% by next peak, $2B cost savings by FY2027.
FedEx Freight spin-off on track for June 1, 2026, expected to unlock value.
Strategic collaboration with ServiceNow to monetize logistics data.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: CEO Raj Subramaniam stated 'FedEx delivered an outstanding second quarter as we successfully executed our growth strategy and advanced our network transformation, while navigating a highly challenging external environment,' and CFO John Dietrich said 'Our strong second quarter results and revised full-year outlook reflect the momentum that is building in our business.'
